key_insight: A deep neural operator learns the mapping from problem inputs to both the PDE solution and the evolving free boundary, delivering high-precision predictions fast enough for real‑time applications such as tumour growth simulation.
problem_solved: Overcomes the computational cost, limited generalization, and numerical complexity of traditional solvers for free boundary problems (moving interfaces coupled to PDEs), enabling accurate, fast predictions across varied parameters and initial conditions.
method: Train a deep neural operator that maps inputs (initial/boundary conditions, model parameters) directly to spatio‑temporal solution fields and the location/evolution of the free boundary.

Use supervised data (synthetic/solver-generated) with architecture and loss design that capture the coupling between PDE dynamics and interface motion; optionally incorporate physics-based regularization for stability and fidelity.
Optimize for efficient inference so the model supports real‑time simulation, parameter sweeps, and rapid uncertainty analysis.
impact: Provides ML practitioners a scalable surrogate approach for PDEs with moving boundaries, unlocking real‑time simulation, faster model-based clinical decision support (e.g., tumour growth), and efficient downstream tasks like sensitivity analysis and control.

paper_title: Deep neural operator for free boundary problems
